_doc: Judgments written before any computed novelty or relevance was seen. novelty: N = new information (the result shows structure that the observations of what it reads don't show: topology, geometry, a match between tables, a selection whose shape is new); R = re-encoding (summaries, regroupings, orders, set differences, translations, frames, bounding boxes, arithmetic of what the reads show); ? = unsure. relevance: Y = bears on the output beyond the input grid; N = doesn't; ? = unsure. Task-wide tables (DETs, constant across input worlds) are not judged.

&bg_cell: figure/ground: the shape of the background region is new; the fill cells are among them
&outside.source: background cells on the grid edge: a simple geometric filter
&outside.reached: flood: reachability from the edge is not shown by the background cells' observations
&enclosed: set difference of background cells and reached cells; these are the cells to fill
&output: re-encodes enclosed cells with the fill color over the input

&body_count.size: counts per color of the ink cells
&body.maximal: order over counts; marks the body color
&mark: ink cells not of the largest color: a set difference
&cast_dir: which side of the box the mark faces: a geometric relation between two tables
&beam: ray cells on the background, colored by the mark: a filter and recolor of the rays

&biggest_count.size: size of each component: a summary of the components
&biggest.maximal: order over sizes; its color is the output color

&peel.boundary: the grid edge: given by the grid size
&peel_depth.distance: depth of each cell from the edge: a function of the grid size
&peel_depth.predecessor: a function of the grid size
&rings.rank: order over depths; maps a ring to its reversed ring
&ring_color: one color per ring: the concentric structure is new

&panel: the color around the holes: a relation between holes and the input
&panel_box.box: bounding box of the panel color
&shape: figure/ground: cells not background and not the panel color
&fits.superset: match of shapes to holes by footprint
&fits.equal: match of shapes to holes by footprint
&output: the panel cropped, with matched shapes in the holes

&moved: input cells translated by a task-wide offset
&output: the moved cells over the background

&pack.distance: how far each mover cell travels before it is blocked
&output: the landed cells over the input

&figure: object cells in box coordinates: a normalization
&inv.conflict: which objects conflict under which symmetry

&taxicab: Manhattan distance to the seed: a function of the seed position and the grid size
&nearest.rank: order per cell over seeds; trivial with one seed
&hue: color by distance along the cycle

&frame_box.box: bounding box of the frame color
&hole.box: bounding box of the cells inside the frame box
&object_cell: figure/ground: cells not background and not the frame color
&output: the frame with the scaled object
